value.body: State animal husbandry departments employ veterinary officers (also called veterinary assistant surgeons) to run veterinary hospitals and dispensaries. The work covers treating livestock and pets, vaccination drives, artificial insemination programmes, disease surveillance and delivering state and central livestock schemes, mostly in rural areas.

items.label: Basic requirement
items.note: Registration with the State Veterinary Council / Veterinary Council of India

items.label: Who recruits
items.value: State PSCs or the animal husbandry department
items.note: Some states also hire on contract

items.label: Veterinary hospitals and polyclinics
items.note: Plus ~30,200 dispensaries and ~24,500 aid centres, mostly run by state governments
items.source: Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Rajya Sabha reply (as reported)

items.label: BVSc & AH enrolment
items.note: All years of the course; based on actual institutional responses

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Complete the BVSc & AH (5.5 years including internship) and register as a veterinary practitioner. Then apply for the state's veterinary officer recruitment — usually a PSC written exam and/or interview; some states recruit on merit plus interview. Knowledge of the state language is often required.

value.title: At a glance
items: Recruitment is state by state and irregular.
Postings are often in rural blocks, with field visits as a routine part of the job.
Promotion leads to senior and district-level animal husbandry posts; an MVSc can help for specialist and teaching roles.

value.title: BVSc & AH enrolment
value.note: Counts students across all years of the degree, not annual intake. A separate 'B.V.Sc.' row (~4,300–5,400) is not included. Based on actual responses from institutions that reported data; the true national figure is likely somewhat higher.
